heading: Rust, Go and C# on the web
body: A service written only in Rust, only in Go or only in C# needs no browser sibling on the web. Rust links on the three desktops, C# links on Windows, and Go links on no host. Where a host links the service, it runs natively. Everywhere else, including the web, it runs as WebAssembly: in the browser, or in the web view of a native target (ADR 0035, ADR 0037, ADR 0045; an ADR is an architecture decision record). Rust compiles with rustc --target wasm32-unknown-unknown into one small module. Go compiles with GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm into one module for all the Go services of the application. The module carries the Go runtime, so it starts at about 2.7 MB, and the page loads it with Go's own wasm_exec.js. C# publishes onto the .NET browser runtime. That runtime is about 3 MB, and the service worker caches it once. F# services compile into a small F# library that runs on the same .NET browser runtime, so a page with C# and F# services loads that runtime once; no host links F#, so an F# service runs as WebAssembly on every target, Windows included (ADR 0073). So when a service has several of these versions, Tachyon uses Rust, then Go, then C#, then F#. The page speaks the same companion protocol as a native host, so the service is the same file. Its fields render. Its methods take JSON arguments: String, &str, bool, numbers or TacValue in Rust, string, bool, numbers, slices, maps or structs in Go, and string, bool, numbers or object in C# and F#. An F# service shows its `member val` properties and its public members. A view reaches the exported Go members with a lower-case first letter, so Count is {tally.count}. Service and NeedsAll sit on their own lines above the type. Rust spells Service as #[Service], Go spells it as // @Service, C# spells it as [Service], and F# spells it as [<Service>]. A bare constructor lets every field take the property with the same name, and it makes the service one per component. A WebAssembly service has no DOM and no platform. It is state and logic over the properties its tag passes. Those properties may carry a data file of up to 1 MiB. ty doctor checks for the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, Go 1.27 and the .NET wasm-tools workload.
